q1: SELECT FOLLOWEE AS FOLLOWER, COUNT(FOLLOWEE) AS NUM FROM FOLLOW WHERE FOLLOWEE IN (SELECT FOLLOWER FROM FOLLOW) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
q2: SELECT FOLLOWEE AS FOLLOWER, COUNT(1) AS NUM FROM FOLLOW GROUP BY 1 HAVING FOLLOWEE IN (SELECT DISTINCT FOLLOWER FROM FOLLOW) ORDER BY 1
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT FOLLOWEE AS FOLLOWER, COUNT(FOLLOWEE) AS NUM FROM FOLLOW WHERE FOLLOWEE IN (SELECT FOLLOWER FROM FOLLOW) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT FOLLOWEE AS FOLLOWER, COUNT(1) AS NUM FROM FOLLOW GROUP BY 1 HAVING FOLLOWEE IN (SELECT DISTINCT FOLLOWER FROM FOLLOW) ORDER BY 1
explanation: Q1 first filters the rows where FOLLOWEE is in the list of FOLLOWERs, and then groups by FOLLOWEE (aliased as FOLLOWER) to count the number of followers each user has. Q2, on the other hand, groups by FOLLOWEE (aliased as FOLLOWER) and uses a HAVING clause to filter out users who are not in the list of FOLLOWERs. This can lead to different results if there are users who are not following anyone.
counterexample_dsp: A user who is not following anyone will be included in the result of Q2 but not in the result of Q1.
